\section{Overview}
General-input fourth-moment bounds are expressed in polynomial coefficients and coordinate influences.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment in terms of coefficient energy]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_polynomial_fourth_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.independent_multilinear_reasonable, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $(X_i)$ be independent real inputs on a probability space, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Then $\mathbb E[F(X)^4]\le9^k(\sum_S a_S^2)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moment of a coordinate derivative]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_coordinate_fourth_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative_degree, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative_sum_sq, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_polynomial_fourth_moment, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Define $A_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ and $D_i(x)=\sum_{S:i\notin S}a_{S\cup\{i\}}\prod_{j\in S}x_j$. Suppose $F$ has degree at most $k+1$ and $(X_j)$ are independent real inputs on a probability space, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Then $\mathbb E[D_i(X)^4]\le9^k I_i(F)^2$, where $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$.
\end{theorem}
